title: Tensor projection formula for extension by zero on a ringed-site slice
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site, with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $U\in\mathcal C$. Use the localized ringed site $(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal O_U)$ and restriction $\mathcal F|_U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and the categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Define $j_{U!}\mathcal G=(P_{\mathcal G})^\#$, where $P_{\mathcal G}$ is the direct-sum extension-by-zero presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] and $(-)^\#$ is module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For every $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal G$ and every $\mathcal O$-module $\mathcal F$, there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O$-modules, natural in both variables, $$j_{U!}(\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}\mathcal F|_U)\cong (j_{U!}\mathcal G)\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal F,$$ where the tensors are sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

proof.text: Write $T_U(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)=\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$ and $T(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)=\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$. For every $v:V\to U$, the relocalization $(\mathcal C/U)/(V/U)\cong\mathcal C/V$ identifies the restricted modules and their scalar actions sectionwise. Hence both $T(\mathcal F,\mathcal H)|_U(V/U)$ and $T_U(\mathcal F|_U,\mathcal H|_U)(V/U)$ are the same set of $\mathcal O_V$-linear maps $\mathcal F|_V\to\mathcal H|_V$. The identification keeps every component of each map. Restriction along $W\to V$ is restriction of those components on both sides, and scalar multiplication is postcomposition with the same multiplication map. This gives an isomorphism $c_{\mathcal F,\mathcal H}:T_U(\mathcal F|_U,\mathcal H|_U)\cong T(\mathcal F,\mathcal H)|_U$. Precomposition by $f$ and postcomposition by $h$ commute with $c$, since both give componentwise $h\circ\varphi\circ f$.

proof.text: Put $A=j_{U!}(\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}\mathcal F|_U)$ and $B=(j_{U!}\mathcal G)\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal F$. For an arbitrary test module $\mathcal H$, the extension adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(A,\mathcal H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal F|_U,\mathcal H|_U)$. Apply the tensor-Hom bijection on the slice, using its symmetry to put $\mathcal F|_U$ in the fixed tensor factor, to obtain $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal G,T_U(\mathcal F|_U,\mathcal H|_U))$. These bijections are natural in $\mathcal G,\mathcal F,\mathcal H$.

Postcompose with $c_{\mathcal F,\mathcal H}$ from step 1. This gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal G,T(\mathcal F,\mathcal H)|_U)$. Use the inverse extension-adjunction bijection to obtain $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(j_{U!}\mathcal G,T(\mathcal F,\mathcal H))$, and the inverse tensor-Hom bijection (again with symmetry) to obtain $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(B,\mathcal H)$. Denote the composite of steps 2 and 3 by $E_{\mathcal G,\mathcal F,\mathcal H}:\operatorname{Hom}(A,\mathcal H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B,\mathcal H)$. Each component is natural: the two adjunctions have the naturality stated in the cited nodes, and step 1 verifies it for $c$. Thus $E$ commutes with postcomposition in $\mathcal H$ and precomposition by the induced maps of $A$ and $B$ in the parameters.

Here is the representability argument explicitly, without an additional lemma. Set $u=E_{\mathcal G,\mathcal F,A}(\mathrm{id}_A):B\to A$ and $v=E_{\mathcal G,\mathcal F,B}^{-1}(\mathrm{id}_B):A\to B$. Naturality in the test module implies $E_{\mathcal G,\mathcal F,\mathcal H}(q)=q\circ u$ for every $q:A\to\mathcal H$ and $E_{\mathcal G,\mathcal F,\mathcal H}^{-1}(r)=r\circ v$ for every $r:B\to\mathcal H$. Evaluating the two inverse identities at $\mathrm{id}_A$ and $\mathrm{id}_B$ gives $u\circ v=\mathrm{id}_A$ and $v\circ u=\mathrm{id}_B$. Consequently $v:A\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ is the required isomorphism of module sheaves.

For maps $g:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G^\prime$ and $f:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F^\prime$, write $a:A\to A^\prime$ and $b:B\to B^\prime$ for the induced maps. Parameter naturality of $E$ gives $E_{\mathcal G,\mathcal F,A^\prime}(a)=E_{\mathcal G^\prime,\mathcal F^\prime,A^\prime}(\mathrm{id}_{A^\prime})\circ b=u^\prime\circ b$. Test-module naturality gives the same left side as $a\circ u$. Using $u\circ v=\mathrm{id}_A$ and $v^\prime\circ u^\prime=\mathrm{id}_{B^\prime}$ gives explicitly $v^\prime\circ a=v^\prime\circ a\circ u\circ v=v^\prime\circ u^\prime\circ b\circ v=b\circ v$. This is naturality in both variables, including simultaneous morphisms, and completes the statement.
